author: ribeye
dek: Google's new flagship AI model is out — for paying customers only, at a price that doubles in November — and a Middletown family is already doing the math.
disclaimer: Parody: the Whitaker family of Middletown is fictional. Google releasing Gemini 4 Argon is real, as reported by Reuters in October 2026.
headline: Google Unleashes Gemini 4 Argon, and a Middletown Dad Immediately Asks What It Costs Per Million

ohio_story: MIDDLETOWN, Ohio — Dan Whitaker did everything right. He read the announcement twice, he checked the price, he even watched a video of a man building a 3D temple on his laptop before dinner. Then he sat down at the kitchen table in Middletown, opened his laptop, and discovered the catch in Google's shiny new flagship AI model, Gemini 4 Argon: it was available to developers and businesses, and to paying Pro and Ultra subscribers — and Dan Whitaker, of Middletown, Ohio, is on the free plan.

"It can do my taxes, my coding, and my fantasy football lineup, but it can't do it for free, and the price doubles after November," Dan said, staring at the pricing page the way other men stare at a high-school football scoreboard on a Friday night. "That's the most Ohio thing I've ever heard about a robot." His wife, Carla, a teacher at Middletown High, had asked the model to plan her week and gotten back a spreadsheet; she asked it for a meatloaf recipe and, Dan swears, it gave her a supply-chain analysis. The kids, meanwhile, have already decided Argon is their new homework helper, a plan Carla describes as "absolutely not happening" and Dan describes as "let's see what it charges first."

By Thursday, Dan had done the math the way only a Middletown dad with a calculator and a pot of coffee can do it: at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, his little side project would cost less than a Skyline coney run — until Dec. 1, when the price doubles to $4 and $20 and suddenly the robot costs more than the groceries. He has now set a calendar reminder for Nov. 30, printed out the pricing page, and taped it to the fridge next to the Middies football schedule. "The Buckeyes don't double their ticket prices in November," he said, "and neither should my chatbot."
real_summary: Google on Wednesday, Oct. 13, 2026, released its flagship AI model Gemini 4 Argon to developers and businesses worldwide, seeking to regain ground against rivals OpenAI and Anthropic after months of delays and a leadership shakeup at its DeepMind lab. Google said the model excels at "deep work" on complex, multi-step tasks in coding, finance, law, cybersecurity and science.

Argon is available to paying customers through Google's AI application-building tools. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can access it through the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, while the Antigravity coding tool is limited to Ultra subscribers. API pricing at launch starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with rates set to double after November 30. Google said teams using Argon in Antigravity increased agentic code submissions by more than 35%, while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third.

The release followed a rocky stretch for Google's AI efforts. The company announced in September that it no longer planned to release Gemini 3.5 Pro, which CEO Sundar Pichai had originally said would be released in June, and it overhauled DeepMind after co-founder and CEO Demis Hassabis stepped aside and several leaders of its Gemini model left the company. Argon had first been announced on Sept. 30 with access limited to a small set of trusted cybersecurity partners through Google's Fairwind Program; Google said it would now open that program to hundreds of additional partners, and offer 10,000 scientists six months of free access to Antigravity's highest usage tier.
source_note: Reuters reporting, Oct 2026: Google releases flagship AI model Gemini 4 Argon to developers and businesses worldwide on Oct. 13, with launch API pricing and access tiers.
